name: Wave Hill
funding: FY2025 expenses $9.4M; 26% government (city-owned site), 31% contributions and grants, 25% investment income.
watch: No adverse finding; supporters roster not checked. FY25 report names only the board and Leadership Council (none flagged); corporate, foundation and government funders not named.
records_note: Posts the FY2025 annual report with a financial summary, its 2025 Form 990 and a named board; no donor list is published.

name: MOCA Cleveland
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies gives lead institutional support. In 2020 the museum cancelled Shaun Leonardo's show; it later apologised and the director resigned.
why_flagged: Bloomberg Philanthropies gives lead institutional support. In 2020 the museum cancelled Shaun Leonardo's show; it later apologised and the director resigned.
records_note: Its Form 990 is public for 2001 to 2025, it names institutional supporters undated and lists its board; no annual reports found.

name: Columbus Museum of Art
funding: Columbus Foundation funds give ongoing support; JPMorgan Chase backs its Center for Creativity; the Pizzuti family gave its Park Street building in 2018. No donor list was found.
watch: An archive profile says Les Wexner paid for a site study and would give if the museum improved its planning. No gift is documented.
records_note: Its About page links a FY25 impact report and a Form 990 copy, names 18 trustees and shows funder logos undated.

name: Wadsworth Atheneum Museum of Art
funding: $18.8M expenses (2023); FY2024: Travelers, Hartford Foundation, CT DECD, Henkel, Lincoln Financial, Bank of America, estates.
watch: No adverse finding; roster not checked. Viking Fuel Oil Co. (heating-oil dealer, $500-1,499 tier) on FY2024 list. Ex-employee sued, saying she was fired for questioning a DEI initiative.
records_note: Annual reports 2009 to 2024 and Form 990s on its site, a FY24 philanthropy list naming donors, and a Board of Trustees page.

name: Madison Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: $2.9M expenses (2023); private donors and members; free admission.
watch: Ho-Chunk Gaming Madison, a casino, sponsors Art Fair on the Square. Separate 2022 Triennial racism row. Business Council list is not published.
why_flagged: Ho-Chunk Gaming Madison, a casino, sponsors Art Fair on the Square. Separate 2022 Triennial racism row. Business Council list is not published.
records_note: Its Form 990 is public for 2001 to 2025, it names Art Fair sponsors for 2025 and lists its trustees, but posts no annual reports.

name: El Museo del Barrio
funding: Ford Foundation and MacKenzie Scott lead (2024 list); NYC/NYSCA public money, banks (BofA, Morgan Stanley), Maestro Dobel tequila.
watch: Neither finances nor roster verified. Bloomberg Philanthropies on roster (plus Bloomberg Connects). Activists protested the museum's mission at its 50th, June 2019. Roster is an Aug 2024 archive copy; live page 403.
records_note: No annual reports found; 990s are on ProPublica, a 2024 supporters list names donors by giving tier, and trustees are listed.

name: Morgan Library & Museum
funding: $31.4M expenses (2023); J.P. Morgan endowment, JPMorgan Chase (top corporate donor), Morgan Stanley, AIG, law firms, NYC and NYS funds.
watch: Banking founding fortune; current roster not checked. Bloomberg Philanthropies is a Leader-level corporate supporter (list current as of 28 Jul 2025). Read via Wayback; site returns 403.
records_note: Annual Reports to Donors run 2004 to 2024, a dated corporate supporter roster is public, trustees are listed, and 990s are on ProPublica.

name: Museum of Arts and Design
funding: $13.7M expenses (2023); private donors, NYSCA and NYC Cultural Affairs, exhibition patrons such as Sarah Arison and Duggal.
watch: No adverse finding; roster not checked. Ex-CFO sued in Mar 2024, saying she was fired for flagging director's expenses. No institutional donor roster published.
records_note: Annual reports for 2008 and 2009 and audited accounts for 2013 to 2019 are on its site; no donor list; trustees are listed.

name: Neue Galerie New York
funding: $20.5M expenses (2023); founder Ronald Lauder (Estée Lauder cosmetics fortune) and admissions.
watch: Founder Ronald Lauder was the target of pro-Palestine protests at MoMA (2021, Nov 2024). Merging into the Met in 2028 (announced 14 May 2026).
why_flagged: Founded by Ronald Lauder, its president. Corporate members: Estée Lauder Companies, Gagosian and Orentreich Family Foundation at $25,000+; Bloomberg Philanthropies at $10,000+. It merges into the Met in 2028.
records_note: It posts no reports or accounts; its Form 990-PF filings are on ProPublica, and its site names corporate members without a date.
other_findings: Epstein link · Ronald Lauder · documented: Ronald Lauder founded the Neue Galerie, which says it co-owns Kirchner's Berlin Street Scene with a private collection. ARTnews describes a 2016 document in the DOJ files as a list of Leon Black's art holdings, including a 50% stake in a Kirchner of that name valued at about $50 million, but it does not confirm that Black is the museum's co-owner. Lauder is mentioned more than 900 times in the January 2026 files, where his and Epstein's assistants arranged meals and calls in 2017; ARTnews found no direct communication between the two men. Lauder has not commented publicly.

name: The Drawing Center
funding: $3.5M expenses (2023); Toll family, Warhol/Mellon/Frankenthaler foundations, NYC DCLA and NYSCA, galleries, UNIQLO.
watch: No adverse finding; roster not checked. Bloomberg Philanthropies in top donor tier (Jul 2023-Jan 2025). 2005: Gov. Pataki pushed it out of the Ground Zero site over its programming.
records_note: No annual reports found; 990s are on ProPublica, the donors page names $1,000+ donors to January 2025, and the board is listed.

name: Chrysler Museum of Art
funding: $18.4M expenses (2023); City of Norfolk plus private donors; founding gift from Walter Chrysler Jr (car fortune).
watch: Newport News Shipbuilding, which builds US Navy carriers and submarines, is a current $5,000 corporate partner. No protest found.
why_flagged: Newport News Shipbuilding, which builds US Navy carriers and submarines, is a current $5,000 corporate partner. No protest found.
records_note: It posts audited statements from 2016 to 2025 with Form 990s, names corporate partners by level and lists its trustees for 2026 to 2027.

name: Joslyn Art Museum
funding: $11.3M expenses (2023); Joslyn endowment (newspaper-syndicate fortune) and private donors.
watch: 2024 pavilion named for Tenaska (natural gas) founder Howard Hawks; uses Bloomberg Connects. No donor roster published; no protest found.
why_flagged: 2024 pavilion named for Tenaska (natural gas) founder Howard Hawks; uses Bloomberg Connects. No donor roster published; no protest found.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts or donor list; Form 990s for 2001 to 2024 are on ProPublica, and its Board of Governors is named.
